will indeed appear in the swaps. However, now two different decompositions will often lead
to the same swap. So how do we account for the overcounting?
   How many times will a given ℓ-sized swap S for T occur? This is equivalent to asking how
many ways can A be split into ℓ subsets where Aj contains αj ? If A has k elements then
there are k − ℓ elements that can be distributed arbitrarily into ℓ sets. This can happen in
ℓ(k−ℓ) ways. Similarly for B. Taking into account permutations we end up with a multiplicity
of ℓ!2 ℓ2(k−ℓ) .
